newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-WEEK AHEAD-Australian markets hang on GDP.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-WEEK AHEAD-Australian markets hang on GDP.

text.p: With little expected from the Reserve Bank board meeting on Tuesday, all eyes will be on September quarter GDP data on Wednesday for clues to the direction of Australian markets into the first quarter of 1997.

A Reuters survey taken on Friday showed economists gave only a 10 percent chance of an easing after Tuesday's RBA meeting, although the 29 economists surveyed indicated a 50 percent chance of an easing in the March quarter next year.
The economists median and average forecast for growth in GDP (A) for the Septemer quarter is 0.6 percent.
Ahead of the GDP data, retail sales and building approvals data for October will be released on Monday, along with September quarter stocks (inventories) data from the Bureau of Statistics.

"Evidence of weak retail spending together with modest GDP growth will maintain the perception that a further easing of monetary policy is necessary," Colonial State Bank economist Hans Kunnen said in a weekly commentary.
Kunnen expects GDP (A) to show a rise of 0.7 percent for the quarter for an annual rate of 3.1 percent.

However, GIO Australia economist Akis Haralabopoulos, who also sees a rise of 0.7 percent for the quarter, said the key statistics for policy makers are labor productivity and alternative measures of inflation.
"Policy makers are likely to be encouraged by the overall economy continuing to grow at a respectible rate," he said.

AUSTRALIAN BONDS (Fri 10-yr cash 7.30 pct, 3-yr 6.61 pct) The Australian bond market will need to see a fairly modest outcome to this Wednesday's third quarter GDP if it is to resume the recent strong rally this week.
The market ended last week under a cloud with the interest rate outlook less clear after recent mildly hawkish comments by Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane and firm data.
Ten year bond yields brushed 7.25 percent on Friday, having brushed just below 7.0 percent at the start of the week.

Dresdner Australia economist Rob Henderson expects GDP (A) to come in just under 0.5 percent for the quarter, making for four quarters growth of 2.9 percent, and he said this could be bullish for the credit market.

"Although this is a backward looking growth figure, with activity slipping below the three percent mark, it seems likely that this news will be bullish for interest rates markets," he said in a weekly commentary.
The market should get off to a good start afte U.S. Treasuries closed sharply higher on Friday but trading was thin following the Thanksgiving Day holiday.
The yield on the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond closed at 6.36 percent compared with a pre-holiday close of 6.43 percent - its lowest close since closing at 6.34 percent on March 4.
The market was helped by a strengthening U.S. dollar, month-end buying and short-covering.
AUSTRALIAN DOLLAR (Fri close US$0.8106/11, NY $0.8160/67)
The Australian dollar looks set to maintain its recent form after rising in overseas trading over the weekend.

Sentiment remains very bullish on the currency following its break of six-year old resistance at US$0.8050 and technical watchers are predicting a rise to US$0.8240 before year-end and evetually US$0.8450, perhaps as soon as January.
Immediate resistance lies in the US$0.8130/50 area with traders reporting sizeable options-related offers, while support has proved solid at US$0.8070/80.

The currency was also expected to maintain its rising trend against the yen since a sluggish Japanese economy has quashed fears of a policy tightening there and should ensure continuing Japanese demand for higher yielding yen/A$ dual currency bonds.
Reactions to the GDP data will be coloured by whether the market thinks they make another rate cut more, or less likely.
Thus weak numbers could take some shine off the currency while a strength, particularly in retail sales and building approvals, might give it the boost needed to clear US$0.8130.
AUSTRALIAN SHARES (Friday All Ords close 2388.6, up 2.3)

Traders see no real trend emerging in the coming week for the equity market with little corporate news expected and only major moves from Wall Street expected to impact a market heading looking beset by pre-Christmas lethargy.
Wall Street continued its strong run on Friday, pushing the Dow Jones Industrial Average 22.36 points higher to 6521.70.
"There is not very much in the way of news we will be watching for," a Brisbane dealer said.
"There is not much on the go," he said.
Traders will also be keeping an eye on stocks with interests in South Australia's Gawler Craton gold province after a strong run up in prices last week.
The sector star, Helix Resources, rose A$1.65 last week to finish at A$3.35 after hitting a high of A$4.15 as "spec fever" hit the market following some promising drilling results.

Among scheduled events, Macquarie Bank releases half year results on Monday and James Hardie Industries on Friday. Annual meetings include George Weston Foods on Tuesday and Bank of Queensland on Thursday.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
